title: STEM Characterization of Substrate/Graphene Epitaxial Influences on GdAuGe Orientations and Interfaces
content: Graphene enables (quasi) Van der Waals (VdW) epitaxy, a synthesis technique which circumvents strict epitaxial lattice matching requirements [1]. Growth following VdW mechanisms is epitaxially registered to graphene. Due to graphene’s thin structure and lack of polar bonds, substrate polar interactions may transmit through the sheet [2]. The simplest interpretation of remote epitaxy assumes that remote substrate interactions permeate through the graphene and epitaxially seeds growth [3, 4]. Though too thick of a graphene stack can obscure remote epitaxy, “long-range” interactions may still be present [5, 6]. Buffer graphene adopts a long-range corrugated structure on 6H-SiC (0001) and modulates the substrate’s surface, which is subject to change with growth of epitaxial graphene layers [7]. We suspect that in the case of GdAuGe growth on buffer graphene/SiC, a graphene-induced surface reconstruction on SiC induces a 30 degree rotated epitaxial GdAuGe film, compared to growth on unreconstructed graphene/SiC that produces an unrotated epitaxial relationship.
